This integration connects a **DSC PowerSeries** or **Honeywell / Ademco
Vista** alarm panel fitted with an **Envisalink EVL-3 or EVL-4** module to
Gladys, locally, through the module's TPI interface (TCP port 4025), without
the EyezOn cloud. Unofficial, not affiliated with EyezOn, DSC or Honeywell.

> **Never tested on a real module.** This version was written from the
> EyezOn TPI documentation and the pyenvisalink library, and tested only
> against a simulated module. Try it first with the panel disarmed, watching
> the logs, and report what differs in the
> [GitHub issues](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-envisalink/issues). Do
> not rely on it as your only intrusion or fire alert.

## What you get

- **One device per partition**, "Alarm partition N": the **mode** (disarmed,
  armed away, armed stay, armed night), **alarm in progress** and **ready to
  arm**. The mode can be set from the dashboard or a scene.
- **One device per zone**: open / closed (or motion, smoke, water leak
  depending on the chosen kind), **alarm**, **tamper**, **fault**.
- **The panel**: Envisalink connected, mains power, low battery, tamper,
  system trouble, panic alarm.
- **Scene triggers**: "Envisalink alarm triggered" (with its kind:
  intrusion or water leak from the kind of the zone in alarm, fire, medical,
  panic, duress, or "partition in alarm, cause unknown" when the zone is not
  configured), "Envisalink partition armed" (with the mode, the user number
  when known, and whether Gladys asked for it), "Envisalink partition
  disarmed".
- **Scene actions**: arm, disarm (if allowed), panic alarm (if allowed).

## Before you start

1. The Envisalink must be on your local network with a fixed address (a DHCP
   reservation in your router).
2. Note the **password of the module's local web page** ("user" by default).
   It is not your EyezOn account password.
3. **One TPI connection at a time**: if Home Assistant, another Gladys or
   another program already uses the module, stop it, or both will keep
   kicking each other out. Sharing the module between programs needs a relay
   such as envisalink-proxy.

## Configuration

1. **Address of the Envisalink**: its IP (e.g. `192.168.1.40`), optionally
   with the port (`192.168.1.40:4025`).
2. **TPI port**: 4025 unless changed.
3. **Envisalink password**.
4. **Alarm panel**: leave "Automatic" (DSC and Honeywell are recognised from
   the module's first message).
5. **Number of partitions**: 1 in most homes.
6. **Zones** (optional): the zones to show from the start, with a name and a
   kind, separated by commas:
   `1=Front door, 2=Hall:motion, 5=Kitchen:smoke, 6=Laundry:leak, 10-12`.
   Kinds: `opening` (default), `motion`, `smoke`, `leak`. A zone the panel
   reports that is not in the list is added by itself, as an opening.
   Changing the kind of a zone creates a new feature: add it again from the
   Discovery tab.
7. Save, then add the devices from the **Discovery** tab.

The **Test the connection** button reconnects at once, asks the panel for its
full status (DSC) and shows the mode of each partition.

## Safety

- **Arming** is allowed by default ("Allow arming" option).
- **Disarming is off by default.** Turn on "Allow disarming" only if your
  Gladys is well protected: anyone who can control your devices will be able
  to disarm the alarm.
- **Panic alarms** from Gladys are off by default.
- **User code**: DSC 4 or 6 digits, Honeywell 4 digits. Needed to disarm,
  and to arm a Honeywell panel or a DSC panel without "quick arm". A
  dedicated code is best. It is never written in the logs, nor is the
  password. Every command (sent or refused) is logged.
- A DSC panel asking for a code while arming (message 900) only gets it
  within 20 seconds of a Gladys command, and only for the partition armed.

### Beware of false alarms

- **Night mode arms without entry delay**: opening the door sets the alarm
  off at once, with no time to type the code. Arm it from a scene only when
  nobody is due to come in.
- **If your panel reports to a monitoring station**, an alarm set off by a
  badly tuned scene, or a panic alarm sent from Gladys, is reported like a
  real one: warn your monitoring company before testing, or put the panel in
  test mode.

## Modes

| Gladys mode | DSC                          | Honeywell          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Armed away  | command 030                  | code + 2 (Away)    |
| Armed stay  | command 031                  | code + 3 (Stay)    |
| Armed night | command 032 (no entry delay) | code + 7 (Instant) |
| Disarmed    | command 040 + code           | code + 1 (Off)     |

To go from one armed mode to another, disarm first.

## Known limits

- Honeywell: the panel reports zones only through the virtual keypad display
  and a bitfield that is not always sent. A zone shown "FAULT", "CHECK" or
  "ALARM" on the keypad goes back to normal when the keypad has not shown it
  for 45 s, or as soon as the partition is "ready" (except the alarm, cleared
  by the disarm). An "ALARM" shown by a disarmed keypad (alarm memory) is not
  an alarm.
- Honeywell, panel armed: the keypad no longer shows the faults. A door left
  open while arming therefore shows **closed after 45 s**, unless the panel
  reports it in its zone bitfield (`%01`). Do not rely on the opening states
  of an armed Honeywell panel.
- Honeywell: a partition shows **armed from the start of the exit delay**
  (the keypad icons light at once), while a DSC panel shows it at the end of
  the delay. The "Partition armed" trigger therefore fires earlier on
  Honeywell.
- Honeywell: **the panic alarm is experimental**: it sends the keypad key A
  (fire), B (medical) or C (police), whose effect depends on the programming
  of your panel.
- The state of a zone shows from its first change (or the panel's first full
  status).
- The Gladys limits (300 states and 300 events per minute) are respected:
  only values that change are sent (plus a reminder about every 30 minutes);
  over 240 states a minute, the zones wait for the next minute while the
  panel and the partitions keep their share; over 120 scene events a minute,
  they are dropped and logged, except "Envisalink alarm triggered", never
  dropped and sent again up to 3 times on an error.

## Troubleshooting

- "Envisalink unreachable": check the address, that the module answers (its
  local web page), and that no other program is connected to port 4025.
- "another client may be using the TPI": the connection drops right after
  the login several times in a row; the integration then waits 5 minutes
  between two tries. Stop the other program, or use a relay
  (envisalink-proxy).
- "refused the password": after three refusals the connection stops so as
  not to lock the module. Fix the password, then save or click "Test the
  connection".
- The link is checked by a keep-alive every minute; with no answer for 3
  minutes, the integration reconnects (5 s, 10 s, 30 s, 1 min, 2 min, then
  every 5 min).

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Envisalink (DSC, Honeywell) asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Envisalink module | `section` | No | For DSC PowerSeries and Honeywell / Ademco Vista alarm panels fitted with an Envisalink EVL-3 or EVL-4 module, on your network, without the EyezOn cloud: the state of each partition (disarmed, armed away, stay or night, in alarm, ready), the zones (open or closed, alarm, tamper, fault), the system troubles (mains, battery, tamper), panic alarms, arming from Gladys and scene triggers. The module accepts one local connection (TPI, TCP port 4025) at a time: stop any other software using it (Home Assistant, another Gladys). Unofficial, not affiliated with EyezOn, DSC or Honeywell. |
| Address of the Envisalink | `string` | Yes | Its IP address or name on your network (give it a fixed address in your router). |
| TPI port | `number` | No | 4025 unless you changed it. |
| Envisalink password | `secret` | Yes | The password of the module's local web page ("user" by default), not your EyezOn account. |
| Alarm panel | `select` | No | Found by itself from the first message of the module. Choose it only when the detection fails. |
| Number of partitions | `number` | No | Partitions 1 to N become devices in Gladys (1 for most homes). |
| Zones | `string` | No | Optional: the zones to show from the start, with a name and a kind (opening, motion, smoke, leak), e.g. "1=Front door, 2=Hall:motion, 5=Kitchen:smoke, 10-12". Zones the panel reports are added by themselves as openings. |
| Safety | `section` | No | Anyone who can control the devices in Gladys (dashboard, scenes, the Gladys app) can use the alarm through this integration. Arming is allowed by default. Disarming and panic alarms are off by default: allow them only if your Gladys is well protected. Every command is written in the integration logs; the user code never is. |
| User code of the alarm | `secret` | No | The code you type on the keypad (DSC: 4 or 6 digits, Honeywell: 4 digits). Needed to disarm, and to arm a Honeywell panel or a DSC panel without quick arming. A dedicated user code is best: the panel logs it with each command. |
| Allow arming from Gladys | `boolean` | No |  |
| Allow disarming from Gladys | `boolean` | No | Needs the user code. Disarming also silences an alarm in progress. |
| Allow panic alarms from Gladys | `boolean` | No | The "Envisalink panic alarm" scene action: fire, medical or police, reported to your monitoring station if you have one (a false alarm can bring a patrol). Experimental on Honeywell: the A / B / C keys depend on the panel programming. |
| Language of the device names | `select` | No | Used for the names of the devices, features and modes added from now on. |

## How to install Envisalink (DSC, Honeywell) in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Envisalink (DSC, Honeywell) appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-envisalink:0.1.3`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-envisalink](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-envisalink).

Envisalink (DSC, Honeywell) requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Envisalink (DSC, Honeywell) is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), not by the Gladys core team.
